mcqs.question: A point in a DBSCAN run has too few neighbors within eps to be a core point, and isn't reachable from any core point either. What happens to it?
options: It is forced into the nearest cluster anyway
It becomes its own single-point cluster
The algorithm fails and needs a smaller eps
It is labeled noise and excluded from every cluster
mcqs.explanation: DBSCAN explicitly supports a noise label for points that don't belong to any dense region — that's the whole point of the 'N' in its name. K-means, by contrast, would be forced to assign it to the nearest centroid.

mcqs.question: You set eps far too large for DBSCAN. What's the most likely outcome?
options: Separate clusters merge into one large cluster
The algorithm ignores eps and uses minPts alone
mcqs.explanation: A large eps makes far-apart points count as neighbors, so DBSCAN chains clusters together that should have stayed separate. Too small an eps causes the opposite problem — splitting one cluster into many or turning most points into noise.

mcqs.question: What is the key output difference between a GMM and K-means for a single data point?
options: GMM only works on 2D data; K-means works on any dimension
GMM outputs a probability per cluster; K-means outputs one hard cluster label
GMM requires labeled data; K-means does not
There is no difference in the output format
mcqs.explanation: A GMM's defining feature is soft assignment — a probability distribution over clusters for each point — while K-means always commits to exactly one cluster per point. Both are fully unsupervised; neither requires labels.

mcqs.question: Your clusters are visibly elongated and rotated ellipses, and you want a confidence score per prediction, not just a label. What should you reach for?
options: DBSCAN, because it never needs a fixed k
A Gaussian Mixture Model, because it models elliptical clusters and gives probabilistic assignment
Hierarchical clustering, because it produces a dendrogram
mcqs.explanation: GMMs fit full covariance Gaussians, so they naturally capture elongated, rotated clusters, and their soft assignment directly gives you a per-point confidence score. K-means can't represent ellipses, and DBSCAN and hierarchical clustering don't produce probabilistic confidence scores.
